entities.summary: William Washington was a cavalry officer of the Virginia militia and Continental Army during the American Revolutionary War, who also served on General George Washington's staff during the naval war with France in 1798 and held a final rank of brigadier general. Primarily known as a commander of light dragoons, he led mounted troops in a number of notable battles in the Carolinas during the campaigns of 1780 and 1781. Following the conflict, this William Washington moved to South Carolina, where he married and served in the state legislature as well as led the Seventh Brigade of the South Carolina militia.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a commander of light dragoons in the Continental Army and later as a brigadier general in the South Carolina militia, William Washington played a notable role in several battles during the American Revolutionary War, contributing to the eventual British defeat. His service in the state legislature also highlights his lasting impact on South Carolina's governance.
